REFLECTION.signature: U_info encodes PAIRED-INTRON CONSISTENCY and DONOR-IDENTITY CONFIDENCE, and it is PHASE-INDEPENDENT. Partner-specific ~37x (partner +0.966 [0.827,1.107] vs non-partner +0.026 [0.009,0.045]); donor-specific ~74x (donor +0.964 vs non-site G +0.013 [-0.006,0.036]); strand-symmetric (+1.07/-0.85, overlapping). FLAT across intron mod 3 (1.05/0.84/0.99) AND across annotated splice phase (1.06/0.93/0.99) -- both overlapping. Modestly coding-enriched (coding +1.009 [0.860,1.148] vs noncoding +0.620 [0.309,0.962], overlapping CIs) but clearly PRESENT on noncoding boundaries too.
REFLECTION.interpretation: A donor GT is scored more probable when its SPECIFIC paired acceptor is intact -- not any AG (non-partner ~0), not a global G shift (non-site G ~0). The two flat phase probes rule OUT both 'raw cross-site phase alignment' (intron mod 3) and 'biological boundary-phase representation' (annotated phase): U_info carries site CONSISTENCY, not reading frame. The mild coding enrichment with a real noncoding effect means it is a general splice-boundary-consistency signal lightly enhanced by coding context, not a dedicated coding-frame detector.

intent_check.handoff_to_period3: Sharp, testable lead: C8 shows period-3 is NECESSARY for the donor coupling, yet 1e shows the coupling is PHASE-INDEPENDENT. So period-3's role in this circuit is most likely POSITIONAL ADDRESSING (locating the partner acceptor at the right codon-phased stride) rather than reading-frame computation -- exactly the discrimination the period-3 truth-table (2a: coding-state detector vs raw alignment vs router) targets.
